newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ekran says no clash in Bakun tendering.
newsitem.headline: Ekran says no clash in Bakun tendering.

text.p: Ekran Bhd, the main promoter of giant Bakun hydroelectric dam, said on Tuesday there is no dispute with the project's lead contractor over subcontracting work.

"There is no change in the understanding between ABB and the four companies that we have," Ting Pek Khiing, executive chairman of Ekran, told reporters following the underwriting signing ceremony for Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Bhd (BHEC), the operating company for the dam.
He was referring to ABB Asea Brown Boveri Ltd, which along with Brazil's Companhia Brasileria Projectos o Obras (CBPO) is leading the consortium to construct the dam.
Press reports in the past month said Ekran and ABB had disagreed over the award of the subcontracts.

Four companies controlled by Ting -- Wembley Industries Holdings Bhd, PWE Industries Bhd, Granite Industries Bhd and Pacific Chemicals Bhd -- have been awarded 4.5 billion ringgit (1.79 billion ringgit) for work related to the dam as lead subcontractors to the project.

Including interest costs during construction, the dam, which is scheduled to be finished by the year 2003 is expected to cost 15.5 billion ringgit ($6.18 billion), BHEC said in a statement at the underwriting ceremony.
The developer had earlier put the cost at 13.6 billion rinngit, but that apparently did not include interest costs.
Ting said 2,400 local companies have registered with Ekran to be subcontractors on the project. "These are the companies, not just the four (Ting-related) companies," he added.
The four Ting-related companies would solicit bids for various subcontracts from the 2,400 local firms.
He said at least 40 percent of all the suncontracts would be given to Malaysian companies. "The local Malaysian (companies) will have 40 percent or more participation in the Bakun project," he said.
